slowest_experiments.experiment: V631 exact Markdown and YAML task-contract preflight
Read-only Qwen3.8 lease and orphan-process diagnosis

summary: The milestone completed 2 experiments in 0.3 minutes, with 1 compute-bound entry. The compute-bound lease and orphan-process diagnosis recorded 0.0 minutes, so the available timing does not expose a slow compute path or explain phase costs.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction and rounded task durations do not expose phase-level causes or distinguish active inference from process diagnosis.
Task records do not correlate accelerator and process telemetry with individual experiments, so compute efficiency cannot be independently audited.
No task record states model concurrency or runner identity, so DualGPURunner engagement cannot be audited for parallel-model work.
improvements_suggested: Emit task-owned start, phase, and completion timestamps at sub-minute precision instead of relying on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Attach GPU utilization samples and process ownership to each compute-bound task so active inference can be separated from stale or orphaned allocations.
Run a lease and orphan-process preflight before compute admission and record any safe teardown outcome.
Record model concurrency and runner identity for every compute-bound task; require DualGPURunner only when at least two models run in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add task-scoped phase timing and GPU telemetry to compute receipts.
Add pre-admission lease ownership and orphan-process cleanup checks.
Persist model-concurrency and runner-identity metadata for each compute task.
meta_reflection: A 0.3-minute reconstructed window with a 0.0-minute compute entry cannot support a calibrated positive savings claim, so the estimate remains 0%. Better task-scoped timing and accelerator attribution are the highest-value evidence improvements for the next retrospective.
